title: Independence of Playfair's axiom via Euclidean and Klein models
abstract: Constructs Euclidean and Klein models of a synthetic Hilbert plane, proving that Playfair's axiom is independent of incidence, Pasch order, and congruence axioms, even with Archimedes and Dedekind continuity. Develops reusable coordinate geometry over ordered fields, projective motions, Klein angles and metric, smooth-path length and distance, congruence constructions, and a coordinate curvature calculation. Dedekind continuity replaces Hilbert's maximal completeness axiom; their equivalence is not formalized. Curvature uses Brioschi's formula, and distance uses C1 paths; no identification with Mathlib's Riemannian distance or connection curvature is asserted.

informal.ParallelPostulate.Hilbert.playfair_indep: There exists a Hilbert plane satisfying Archimedes and Dedekind continuity and Playfair's axiom, and there exists another satisfying the same continuity axioms and the negation of Playfair's axiom. The models use real coordinate planes with bounds zero and minus one.
informal.ParallelPostulate.HyperbolicPlane.hyperb: Over any linearly ordered field, for every negative bound and every line in the bounded coordinate plane, infinitely many distinct lines pass through any point of the plane outside that line without meeting it.
informal.ParallelPostulate.HyperbolicPlane.kleinD: For every negative real bound and every pair of points in its plane, the infimum of C1-path lengths in Klein's coordinate metric equals arsinh of the square root of minus the bound times apart, divided by the square root of minus the bound.
informal.ParallelPostulate.HyperbolicPlane.kleinM: For every real bound, Brioschi's coordinate curvature formula applied to the three coefficients of Klein's metric equals that bound at every point of its coordinate plane.
